aboutPage.meta.description: HatchGrab was founded by Dominic Bonini, who created Village Foodie to know which food trucks come to his village. It’s a small company that he runs personally.
aboutPage.meta.title: About us — HatchGrab
aboutPage.story.hatchgrab: The more food trucks I got to know, the more I thought they deserved better tools: something made for a business that is somewhere different every day, not for a restaurant at a fixed address. That’s why I founded HatchGrab.
aboutPage.story.small: It’s a small company and I run it personally. If you get in touch, I will reply to you, not a ticket queue in a support department.
aboutPage.story.village: I live in a village. Food trucks come to us, but I never knew which one and when without digging through Facebook.
aboutPage.story.villageFoodie: So I created Village Foodie — a simple way to check which food trucks are coming to places near you.

landing.does.capacityBody: Set how much you can prepare at once and how long it takes. When a collection time fills up, customers can no longer choose it.
landing.does.devicesBody: On the phone in your apron pocket, the tablet on the counter, the laptop in the food truck — and on the card terminal you already take payments on.
landing.does.lede: Most ordering systems assume a fixed address, reliable wi-fi and the same hours every week. Every week you stand somewhere else, at different times, with weak coverage or none. HatchGrab was created with exactly that in mind.
landing.does.offlineBody: When you lose coverage, online orders pause automatically, so customers won’t place orders you won’t see. Keep taking orders in the app for iPhone, iPad and Android.

landing.does.whatsappBody: “Where are you tonight?” “What desserts do you have?” Your WhatsApp replies while you’re driving to the spot or standing at the grill — based on your menu and schedule. Messenger and Instagram coming soon.
